name: horse sacrifice

attributes.attribute: a white mare was killed and its broth drunk in the rite of Irish inauguration
the marriage of the king to the land goddess as a mare
the center where the king took the land

text: The horse sacrifice was an Irish ritual. The traveler Giraldus Cambrensis put it on record. The rite joined the crowning of the king to a white mare. At the inauguration of the High King at Tara, the banais righe supposedly required the candidate to lie with a white mare. The mare was then killed, cooked in broth, and the king drank it. Often called a barbaric rite, it appears nowhere else in Irish record. Some scholars doubt the story. It echoes a rite of the wider Indo-European world, in which the queen wore the hide of a newly killed mare and lay with the king. The horse wrapped the king and the land together.

okr.objective: Document the Irish horse sacrifice and the kingship rite.
key_results: the rite recounted by Giraldus Cambrensis.
